annotation.title_clean: Bill C-27: An Act to enact the Consumer Privacy Protection Act, the Personal Information and Data Protection Tribunal Act and the Artificial Intelligence and Data Act and to make consequential and related amendments to other Acts (Charter Statement)
annotation.title_en: Bill C-27: An Act to enact the Consumer Privacy Protection Act, the Personal Information and Data Protection Tribunal Act and the Artificial Intelligence and Data Act and to make consequential and related amendments to other Acts (Charter Statement)
named_instruments_referenced: Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms
Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act
annotation.summary_en: Department of Justice Charter Statement on Canada's Bill C-27 (Digital Charter Implementation Act, 2022), which would enact the Consumer Privacy Protection Act, a data protection tribunal and the Artificial Intelligence and Data Act. It assesses consistency with Charter rights: search and seizure, expression and liberty, and justifies limits.
key_provisions_or_claims: Bill C-27 comprises the CPPA, the Personal Information and Data Protection Tribunal Act and AIDA.
AIDA sets common requirements for AI system design, development and use, including mitigating harm and biased output.
AIDA creates offences for unlawful use of personal information in AI and for reckless harmful AI deployment.
Minister's information-gathering powers under AIDA are found consistent with s. 8 of the Charter.
The Minister identified no inconsistency with Charter sections 7 or 2(b).
